name: Alzheimers Disease Module
remarks: Alzheimer's disease from age-gated MCI incidence through mild, moderate and
severe dementia, long-term care and hospice, with stage-specific mortality.
STRUCTURE (Task 4.2, 2026-08-10 -- staged-progression rework built on top of
Task 1.6's containment hotfix, whose mechanisms are all preserved: the age>=65
Guard + 1.5%/yr annual-reroll MCI incidence, the 10%/yr MCI->AD conversion,
post-diagnosis mortality, the memantine re-order guard, and explicit
EncounterEnds at every supersession point):
MCI  --10%/yr-->  mild AD  --40%/yr-->  moderate  --33%/yr-->  severe
community severe --35%/yr--> nursing facility
hospice (via the hospice contract)
Each stage transition is an annual reroll (a ~365-day Delay carrying its own
distributed_transition), never a per-visit-pass roll, so the stated rate is
the realised per-year rate.
STAGE-DURATION CALIBRATION. Per-year transition rates are set from published
stage durations rather than a single flat rate: the Global Deterioration
Scale/FAST literature puts mild dementia (GDS 4) at roughly 2 years,
moderate (GDS 5) at roughly 1.5-2 years and moderately-severe-to-severe
(GDS 6-7) at roughly 2.5 years (Reisberg B, Ferris SH, de Leon MJ, Crook T,
'The Global Deterioration Scale for assessment of primary degenerative
dementia', Am J Psychiatry 1982;139(9):1136-1139; Reisberg B, 'Functional
assessment staging (FAST)', Psychopharmacol Bull 1988;24(4):653-659).
Converting mean durations to annual hazards gives ~40%/yr mild->moderate and
~33%/yr moderate->severe. Stage-specific competing mortality is taken from
the elevated all-cause mortality reported across dementia severity (Todd S,
Barr S, Roberts M, Passmore AP, 'Survival in dementia and predictors of
mortality: a review', Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2013;28(11):1109-1124) and,
for the advanced/long-term-care arm, from Mitchell SL, Teno JM, Kiely DK,
et al., 'The clinical course of advanced dementia', N Engl J Med
2009;361(16):1529-1538 (median survival ~1.3 years after meeting
advanced-dementia criteria). In the mild and moderate stages death is a
single branch (5%/yr and 10%/yr); from the severe stage onward it is split
between dying without hospice (13%/yr community-severe, ~21.7%/yr in
long-term care) and electing hospice first (30%/yr and ~49.7%/yr), because
hospice here is a route to death rather than an additional endpoint.
The resulting mean survival from
AD diagnosis is ~5.6 years by graph arithmetic (see the Task 4.2 report for
the full computation), inside the 4-8 year range the Alzheimer's Association
commonly cites. These are calibration approximations, not literature-exact
replications, and they were NOT fitted to a simulated cohort -- per-task
generation runs are not performed in this lane.
TREATMENT. Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil / rivastigmine / galantamine)
are dispensed prescriptions -- prescribable SCD RxCUIs with chronic:true, so
the engine's chronic-medication renewal keeps refilling them for life
(Birks JS, 'Cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease', Cochrane
Database Syst Rev 2006;(1):CD005593). Memantine is added at the moderate
stage, also chronic and still guarded against re-ordering. Anti-amyloid
antibodies are administered infusions (administration:true -> J-code path,
never the Part D/NDC path) restricted to the early-stage, amyloid-positive
subgroup and given as a bounded course with a real cadence: lecanemab 39
biweekly infusions over ~18 months (van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, et al.,
'Lecanemab in early Alzheimer's disease', N Engl J Med 2023;388(1):9-21) and
donanemab 18 monthly infusions over ~72 weeks (Sims JR, Zimmer JA, Evans CD,
et al., 'Donanemab in early symptomatic Alzheimer disease', JAMA
2023;330(6):512-527), each with periodic ARIA surveillance MRI. Amyloid
positivity is attribute-modelled at 55% of incident MCI, consistent with the
amyloid-PET positivity prevalence reported in MCI populations (Jansen WJ,
Ossenkoppele R, Knol DL, et al., 'Prevalence of cerebral amyloid pathology in
persons without dementia', JAMA 2015;313(19):1924-1938, which reports
positivity rising with age across the MCI range). Only 12% of the
amyloid-positive subgroup starts an antibody, reflecting real-world uptake
limits (eligibility work-up, infusion capacity, APOE4/ARIA risk) rather than
a published uptake figure -- an explicit assumption.
CARE SETTING. The long-term-care phase is a recurring *closed* skilled-nursing
encounter: a bounded 20-30 day covered period inside the encounter, then an
EncounterEnd, then a 60-75 day interval OUTSIDE any encounter. Real nursing
facility residence is continuous, but a continuously-open encounter would hold
the engine's single per-person encounter reservation for the rest of the
patient's life and silently suppress every other module's visits -- the exact
defect class this remediation exists to remove. Sampling residence as
recurring bounded covered periods keeps plausible institutional claim
durations without a lifelong lock. This is a deliberate modelling trade-off,
documented rather than hidden.
HOSPICE. This module does not model hospice encounters itself. It honours the
tree's hospice contract: it sets `hospice_reason` (to its own AD condition
entry) and `hospice` = true, which is what home_hospice_snf.json's own
Alzheimers branch does, and which hospice_treatment.json's `Wait for Hospice`
Guard reads to run the real hospice-class encounter, certification, per-diem
hospice care and discharge. A module-isolated run therefore shows no hospice
encounters from this module; a full-tree run gets them from
hospice_treatment.json with a correct `reason`.
COORDINATION WITH stock dementia.json (Task 5.2, group 2 -- CLOSED). Both
modules diagnose SNOMED 26929004 and had no cross-gating; dementia.json also
diagnoses 230265002 (familial early-onset AD) from the same encounter. The
two are now mutually exclusive, first-to-diagnose wins, gated on both sides:
Stock_Dementia_Dx_Guard / Stock_Dementia_Dx_Recheck here, and
Custom_AD_Dx_Guard / Custom_AD_Dx_Recheck in dementia.json (which tests this
module's `alzheimers_disease` attribute).
The single most damaging consequence this closes is NOT the duplicate
diagnosis -- HealthRecord.conditionStart is idempotent per code, so 26929004
never produced two condition rows -- it is dementia.json's EndFirstPrescription
(MedicationEnd, referenced_by_attribute 'Alzheimer's Medication'). Because
HealthRecord.medicationStart is idempotent per RxCUI, dementia.json's donepezil
997223 / galantamine 310436 orders bound that attribute to THIS module's
already-open chronic order, and the MedicationEnd then ran
HealthRecord.chronicMedicationEnd on it -- deleting the lifelong refill stream
for the ~80% of this module's patients on those two drugs. See
task-4.2-report.md section 5 item 3 and task-5.2-report.md group 2.
What the gate does NOT do: it does not move the Phase 1 gate's combined 65+
26929004 share of 0.166 (vs 0.078 for this module alone). Mutual exclusion
removes overlapping care pathways, not patients -- the union of the two
modules' diagnosed populations is unchanged by construction. That 0.166 is a
calibration question for whoever owns the ceiling, not a coordination bug.
Task 1.6 containment fix, preserved unchanged by Task 4.2: the pre-1.6
module opened MildCognitiveImpairment unconditionally off a fixed
birth-anchored delay chain, so ~100% of the population eventually got MCI.
Entry is gated at 65 and Annual_MCI_Incidence_Check does the per-year
rolling, so the earliest possible onset age is ~66.
Annual reroll loop, not a birth/age roll: the Delay and the
distributed_transition live on the same state, so 1.5% is the realised
per-year incidence. Approximates population-based amnestic-MCI incidence
in adults 65+ (pooled cohort estimates cluster around 1-2 per 100
person-years; Petersen RC, 'Mild Cognitive Impairment', Continuum
(Minneap Minn) 2016;22(2):404-418). Calibration approximation, not a
literature-exact replication.
Task 4.2: the MCI diagnosis, its MoCA and the memory-impairment symptom
used to fire BEFORE this visit opened (Task 1.6 reported them as
clinical states reached with no encounter open and deferred the fix
here). The encounter now opens first, so every clinical row it produces
is attributable to a real visit.
MoCA is 0-30; 18-25 approximates the MCI band.

codes.display: Assessment and interpretation of higher cerebral function, cognitive testing

remarks: Task 1.6 recoded this from CPT 99483 (a bad-system entry the RIF
mapper cannot see). 113024001 is an active SNOMED concept mapped to
99483 in hcpcs_code_map.json, so the CPT billing code survives export.
TASK 6.1 EXPORT-MAP FLAG (recorded here because this module is the row's
only consumer): 113091000's hcpcs_code_map row is [S8035 'Magnetic
source imaging', S8042 'MRI, low-field']. Neither is a payable brain-MRI
code -- brain MRI is CPT 70551 (without contrast) / 70552 (with) /
70553 (without and with). 113091000 is used ONLY in this module, in
three states (BrainMRI, Baseline_ARIA_MRI, ARIA_MRISurveillance), so
6.1 can re-weight or replace the row with no effect on any other
module. Task 4.2 grew the row's traffic (two states to three, and the
anti-amyloid infusion loop fires ARIA_MRISurveillance ~3 times per
treated patient), which raises the value of fixing it.
Amyloid status is attribute-modelled (per the Task 4.2 brief), not
modelled as a PET/CSF procedure -- there is no verified-active SNOMED
amyloid-PET concept with an existing hcpcs_code_map row in this tree,
and inventing one is out of scope. 55% positivity approximates the
amyloid-PET positivity prevalence reported across MCI populations
Only amyloid-positive, early-stage (MCI) patients can reach this state,
which is the labelled population for lecanemab and donanemab. 12% uptake
among eligible patients is an explicit assumption standing in for
real-world access limits (specialist referral, infusion capacity,
APOE4/ARIA risk tolerance), not a published figure. Net effect: ~6.6% of
incident MCI starts an anti-amyloid antibody.
Baseline MRI is required by both antibodies' labels before the first
infusion, to establish ARIA risk.
Reached exactly once per patient (the infusion loop re-enters
Infusion_Visit, not this state), so the agent choice is made once and
then locked into `chosen_biologic`. Task 1.6 introduced that lock to
stop the old loop re-rolling 60/40 and switching a patient's antibody
mid-therapy; the lock is preserved and is now also what routes the
per-agent infusion interval.
CLARITY AD: 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for 18 months = 39 infusions
(van Dyck CH et al., NEJM 2023;388(1):9-21).
TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2: IV every 4 weeks for up to 72 weeks = 18 infusions
Task 1.6 established that the administration must run INSIDE this
encounter (HealthRecord.medicationAdministration calls currentEncounter,
which silently reuses the most recent historical encounter rather than
opening one, so an administration outside an encounter is mis-attributed
rather than merely orphaned). Task 4.2 keeps that ordering and turns the
single visit into a real, counted, per-agent course.
HealthRecord.medicationAdministration builds a NEW Medication entry on
every call (unlike medicationStart, which is idempotent per RxCUI), so
each pass through this loop is a genuine separate administered claim.
administration:true routes this to the J-code path; RxCUI 2626143 has a
rxnorm_hcpcs_map row (J0174, lecanemab-irmb 1 mg) with a single
unweighted entry, so CodeMapper's default weight 1.0 applies and it
cannot mis-bill as another drug. `reason` is the MCI condition, not
`alzheimers_disease`: this arm is early-stage by construction, so the
AD attribute is not set yet (it was previously referenced here and
resolved to nil).
RxCUI 2687966 -> J0175 (donanemab-azbt, 2 mg), single unweighted row.
Both labels require surveillance MRI at a small number of fixed points in
the course (lecanemab before the 5th, 7th and 14th infusions). An 8%
per-infusion probability reproduces roughly that count over a 39-infusion
course without a second counter; it is a frequency approximation, not the
label's exact schedule.
Early discontinuation (symptomatic ARIA, infusion reactions, withdrawal).
1.5% per infusion compounds to ~45% of a 39-infusion lecanemab course
and ~24% of an 18-infusion donanemab course not being completed, the
right order of magnitude for real-world antibody discontinuation; the
per-infusion figure itself is an assumption, not a published rate.
The treated arm spends ~18 months inside the infusion loop, during which
no MCI->AD progression roll fires. That is an incidental consequence of
Synthea's single-threaded module execution, not an explicitly modelled
treatment effect -- but it does displace ~1.5 annual progression rolls,
which points in the same direction as the ~27% slowing of decline
reported in CLARITY AD. Named here so nobody mistakes it for a
calibrated efficacy model.
Task 1.6 replaced the pre-fix 0.5/0.4/0.1 absorbing chain (which sent
~83% of MCI patients to AD) with this annual reroll; Task 4.2 keeps the
rates unchanged. 10%/yr MCI->AD conversion is the fix brief's mandated
rate and is the order of magnitude reported for amnestic MCI in
population-based cohorts; 5%/yr reversion to normal cognition is a
calibration approximation (Petersen RC, Continuum 2016;22(2):404-418).
Reverting patients leave the module permanently (Task 1.6 behaviour,
preserved). Routing them back to Annual_MCI_Incidence_Check would be more
faithful -- MCI reversion is not protective against later MCI -- but it
would let MildCognitiveImpairment fire a second time and stack a
duplicate diagnosis, the Class 8 defect this remediation is removing.
Accepted simplification, named rather than hidden.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 2) -- this module <->
stock dementia.json. Closes the KNOWN COORDINATION GAP recorded in this
module's header remarks and in task-4.2-report.md section 5.
Rule: FIRST-TO-DIAGNOSE WINS. dementia.json records the very same SNOMED
26929004 from its AlzheimersOnset arm, and 230265002 (familial early-onset
AD) from its PreEarlyOnsetAlzheimers arm; both are checked here because
both are a dementia diagnosis on the same patient. If either is already
an Active Condition this module stands down (Terminal) rather than adding
a second, parallel AD care pathway.
This is the only entry point to AD_Diagnosis_Visit -> MildDementia, so
26929004 has exactly one gate on this side.
Terminal, not a return to Annual_MCI_Progression_Check: the patient keeps
the MCI condition this module already gave them and dementia.json owns
their AD course from here (staging, ChEIs, MMSE, hospice via
`Type of Alzheimer's`). Rerouting into the reroll loop would just retry
the same blocked diagnosis every year.
Timing note (why a second check follows the visit): AD_Diagnosis_Visit is
a non-wellness Encounter, and State.Encounter.process returns false --
i.e. blocks across ticks -- while another module holds the person's
encounter lock. So passing this gate does not guarantee the diagnosis
lands in the same tick, and dementia.json could win the race in between.
Stock_Dementia_Dx_Recheck re-tests immediately before MildDementia, where
the chain to the ConditionOnset really is Delay-free and atomic.

codes.display: Familial Alzheimer's disease of early onset (disorder)

remarks: Task 4.2: the AD diagnosis used to fire before its memory-clinic visit
opened (reported by Task 1.6, deferred here). Encounter first now.
CROSS-MODULE GATE, second half (task 5.2 group 2). Same test as
Stock_Dementia_Dx_Guard, re-run after the memory-clinic visit has
actually opened. This is the check that makes the exclusion airtight on
this side: from here to MildDementia there is no Delay and no blocking
state, and module processing is single-threaded per person per tick, so
no other module can diagnose between this test and our ConditionOnset.
Using the CODE (not dementia.json's `Type of Alzheimer's` attribute) is
deliberate: that attribute is set at dementia.json's AlzheimersOnset,
which precedes its diagnosis by years of undiagnosed prodrome, and about
38% of the population passes through that prodrome. Gating on it would
suppress this module for roughly a third of the elderly and would push
the combined 26929004 prevalence BELOW either module's own calibration.
Gating on the recorded diagnosis keeps the union of the two modules
exactly what it was -- see the report for why 5.2 therefore does not, and
cannot, move the Phase 1 gate's 0.166 combined 65+ share.
Cost of a hit here: this patient keeps one ambulatory 'encounter for
problem' with reason = their MCI entry and no further clinical content.
That is a real memory-clinic follow-up visit, so it is left in the record
rather than suppressed.

codes.display: Familial Alzheimer's disease of early onset (disorder)

remarks: Closes the memory-clinic visit opened by AD_Diagnosis_Visit when
Stock_Dementia_Dx_Recheck hands the patient to dementia.json. Required:
leaving the encounter open would hold this person's encounter lock
forever -- the exact Class 6 defect the audit recorded for
high_output_heart_failure.json.
State name kept from the pre-4.2 module because Death_From_Alzheimers'
`condition_onset` references it by name; it is the single AD diagnosis
for the whole disease course, not a mild-stage-specific code. Stage is
carried by the `ad_stage` attribute, deliberately NOT by additional
ConditionOnset states -- adding stage-specific dementia codes would widen
the code universe this module contributes to the double-diagnosis overlap
with stock dementia.json that Task 5.2 has to resolve.
Task 4.2: added chronic:true. Verified 997223 is a prescribable SCD with
a medication_code_map.json row carrying real NDCs, so it exports on the
Part D / PDE path. Without chronic:true the engine's chronic-medication
renewal (State.java:963-966) never sees it and the patient gets exactly
one lifetime fill of a drug taken daily for years.
RxCUI corrected by Task 1.6 from the dose-form-level 373797 to this real
SCD; medication_code_map row added there. Task 4.2 adds chronic:true.
RxCUI corrected by Task 1.6 from the dose-form-level 384641 to this real
SCD (already in medication_code_map). Task 4.2 adds chronic:true.
Explicit close (Task 1.6 fix round 1 added this at the equivalent point;
without it the next annual visit superseded this one at the same
simulated instant and the diagnosis visit exported STOP == START).
Annual reroll for the mild stage. 40%/yr to moderate corresponds to a
~2-year mean mild-stage duration (Reisberg GDS 4). 5%/yr mortality is
the competing all-cause risk at this severity (Todd S et al., Int J
Geriatr Psychiatry 2013). Pre-4.2 this roll lived on a 9-15 month
review loop at 30% per pass, so the realised annual rate did not match
any stated figure.
Task 1.6 recoded this from CPT 96116; 273643004 is active and mapped to
96116 in hcpcs_code_map.json.
Task 4.2: the moderate-stage MoCA and the ADL/behaviour symptoms used to
fire between the stage SetAttribute and this encounter opening (reported
by Task 1.6 as clinical states with no encounter open, deferred here).
They are now all inside the visit.
Task 1.6 containment fix, preserved: stops the annual moderate-stage
visit re-issuing an order for a drug the patient is already on.
Task 4.2: unit was the free-text 'points' here and in the severe-stage
observation; standardised to UCUM {score}, matching the other MoCA
observations in this module.
33%/yr to severe corresponds to a ~2-3 year mean moderate-stage duration
(Reisberg GDS 5-6); 10%/yr competing mortality. Pre-4.2 this was 35% per
9-15 month pass.
Pre-4.2 the severe stage had no annual loop at all: it fired one set of
symptoms and dropped every patient straight into the long-term-care /
hospice branch, so 100% of severe patients were institutionalised within
one pass. It is now an annual cycle with its own review visit,
complication rolls, and competing exits.
Advance care planning is billed once, not at every annual severe-stage
visit -- pre-4.2 the module had two separate ACP Procedure states on the
same path (ACPProcedure and AdvancedCarePlanning_Action_1), both coded
310303002, which double-billed 99497 for 90% of the patients who reached
the palliative branch.
Task 4.2, following Task 2.2's finding: the previous code 310303002
('Advance directive discussion') is INACTIVE in current SNOMED.
713603004 'Advance care planning' is active (verified via Ontoserver
CodeSystem/$lookup, inactive=false) and already carries the same
hcpcs_code_map row -> CPT 99497, so no export-map change is needed and
the billing code is unchanged.
Aspiration pneumonia and injurious falls are the two dominant acute
events in advanced dementia (Mitchell SL et al., NEJM 2009;361:1529-38:
pneumonia and febrile episodes are the commonest complications and carry
the highest 6-month mortality). Rates per severe-stage year are
assumptions of the right order, not published incidences.
Task 1.6 fixed this state's lint CRITICAL (no closer reachable at all,
because its only target was another Encounter and Encounter re-entry
does not satisfy the inpatient-class check). The bounded LOS + explicit
close are preserved; LOS widened to 3-7 days for an aspiration-pneumonia
antibiotic course.
Task 1.6 flagged this as the same zero-duration inpatient pattern it
fixed for AspirationAdmission but left it alone as out of containment
scope (its report, concern 7). Task 4.2 gives it a bounded LOS and an
explicit close.
Task 4.2 recode, reasoning corrected in fix round 1. The previous code
here was 225358003 under the display 'Assessment after fall'. That
display was fabricated: 225358003 is an active concept whose real
SNOMED display is 'Wound care' (Ontoserver CodeSystem/$lookup). Its
hcpcs_code_map row -> G0282 (electrical stimulation for wound care) /
S9097 (home visit for wound care) is therefore CORRECT, and
gallstones.json and injuries.json use that code and row correctly. The
defect was only ever this module's wrong display and wrong choice of
concept -- so the row must NOT be touched by the Task 6.1 sweep.
Fixed by moving to 762993000 'Assessment using Morse Fall Scale'
(verified active via Ontoserver $lookup, Verhoeff-valid), which already
has its own hcpcs_code_map row -> M1069. No new map row needed.
Annual reroll for community-dwelling severe patients. 35%/yr entry into
long-term care, 13%/yr death without hospice, 30%/yr direct hospice
election. Pre-4.2 there was no annual severe cycle: institutionalisation
was effectively certain on the first pass.
HOSPICE RATE, corrected in fix round 1. The rate is set together with
NursingHome_Period_Check's so that ~48% of this module's AD decedents
elect hospice, matching the ~50% hospice use reported among Medicare
dementia decedents. The previous 12%/5% pair gave ~25% and was justified
by the claim that home_hospice_snf.json and hospice_treatment.json add
elections on top. That claim was FALSE and is retracted: this module's
patients cannot reach either external route. home_hospice_snf.json's
Hospice Check gates its Alzheimers branch on `Type of Alzheimer's`,
which only stock dementia.json ever sets; and hospice_treatment.json's
second Guard branch reads `days_until_death`, which LifecycleModule
only writes once Person.DEATHDATE exists (LifecycleModule.java:993-998)
-- this module's Death state kills immediately, so that attribute is
never a usable pre-death predictor here. This module's own election is
therefore the entire rate.
Renormalisation: hospice is a competing ROUTE to death, not an extra
endpoint (every election reaches Death_From_Alzheimers ~55 days later),
so the direct-death branch was cut 20%->13% as the hospice branch rose
12%->30%, and the stay-in-place branch absorbs the rest. Net effect on
the module's calibration: mean survival from AD diagnosis moves from
6.0 to 5.6 years, still inside the cited 4-8 year range, and mean
long-term-care residence moves from 1.9 to 1.2 years, closer to the
~1.3 year median in Mitchell SL et al., NEJM 2009;361:1529-38.
Pre-4.2 this was a single ambulatory-class encounter coded 160734000
with a 60-120 day delay after it. Two problems: the class made a nursing
facility stay export as an office visit, and 160734000 is actually
'Lives in nursing home' (a finding), not the 'Admission to long-term care
facility (procedure)' the display text claimed -- verified via Ontoserver
$lookup. Now encounter_class snf with 45618002 'Skilled nursing facility'
(active, Verhoeff-valid). Encounter codes are not HCPCS-mapped, so no
export-map row is involved.
The stay is a bounded covered period held open across a 20-30 day Delay
(permitted for snf class; the lint only warns above 90 days) and then
explicitly closed, with the inter-period gap outside any encounter. See
the module header for why continuous residence is not modelled as a
continuously-open encounter.
Same code the stock snf/skilled_nursing_facility submodule uses for its
daily nursing care; active per Ontoserver $lookup and already mapped in
hcpcs_code_map.json (G0299/G0300 skilled nursing services).
Per ~92-day cycle (a 20-30 day covered period plus a 60-75 day gap).
Fix round 1 raised hospice election 5% -> 16% per cycle and cut death
without hospice 8.5% -> 6% to renormalise (see Severe_Stage_Annual_Check
for the reasoning and the retraction of the earlier justification).
73% of long-term-care residents now elect hospice before death, and mean
residence is ~1.2 years, close to the ~1.3 year median survival in
advanced dementia reported by Mitchell SL et al., NEJM 2009;361:1529-38
(the previous 1.9 years overshot it). Direct death without hospice is
~21.7%/yr. 4% per cycle routes back through the acute-complication roll
(a hospitalisation from the facility), which returns here via
Severe_Living_Setting_Check and is not an exit.
Pre-election hospice evaluation; mapped to HCPCS G0337 in
hcpcs_code_map.json. Code corrected by Task 1.6 (the previous 305336008
is 'Admission to hospice', the encounter-type code, under a mismatched
display).
Task 4.2: honours the tree's hospice contract instead of modelling
hospice locally. hospice_treatment.json's Hospice_Admission Encounter
carries `reason: hospice_reason`, so this attribute must hold a condition
entry -- `alzheimers_disease` is this module's own ConditionOnset
attribute. This mirrors home_hospice_snf.json's own `Alzheimers` state,
which sets hospice_reason from dementia.json's `Type of Alzheimer's`.
This module does NOT set `Type of Alzheimer's`: that attribute belongs to
stock dementia.json and writing it from here would be a cross-module
contract violation (see the Task 4.2 report's note to Task 5.2).
hospice_treatment.json's `Wait for Hospice` Guard allows on
`hospice == true`; it then opens the hospice-class encounter, runs
certification/notification/assessment/care-plan and per-diem hospice
care for an exponential LOS (mean 22.7 days), and closes it. That module
resets `hospice` to false on discharge, so this flag is a one-shot
election, not a latch.
Time from hospice election to death. Median hospice length of stay in
dementia is a few weeks to a few months; 20-90 days brackets the
hospice_treatment.json LOS distribution (exponential, mean 22.7 days,
capped at 240) so the stock hospice episode has room to run and close
before this module kills the patient.
Single Death state, reached from the mild, moderate, community-severe and
long-term-care annual/periodic checks and from the hospice period. Task
1.6 introduced mortality (the pre-1.6 module had no Death state at all);
Task 4.2 spreads it across the stages instead of concentrating it in one
end-stage arm. AD is the recorded cause of death, so 100% of this
module's deaths carry the diagnosis.
No encounter is open at any of the five call sites: every one of them is
reached from a Delay that sits after an EncounterEnd (verified by the
both-context BFS -- see the report).
Task 5.2: switched from `condition_onset: MildDementia` to
`referenced_by_attribute: alzheimers_disease`, which resolves to the same
26929004 entry in the normal case but is immune to one residual
cross-module effect. State.Death resolves `condition_onset` by scanning
person.record.present for an entry whose `name` equals the state name
(State.java, Death.process). HealthRecord.conditionStart is idempotent per
code, and State.ConditionOnset.diagnose overwrites `entry.name` on the
entry it gets back -- so if dementia.json's deferred AlzheimersOnset is
diagnosed onto our already-present 26929004, the entry is renamed to
'AlzheimersOnset' and the by-name scan finds nothing, silently recording
a death with a NULL cause. The attribute holds the Entry object itself, so
it survives the rename. Safety: `alzheimers_disease` is assigned by
